x: Chiefly due to a clash with the Stock Exchange 7 miles championships, only 29 walkers started, and we were without Stan Vickers, Ray Hall and Dave Stevens.

Eric Hall took the lead, closely followed by George Williams. Eric broke away after half-a-mile and thereafter was in no danger of defeat. 63 sec. up at the half distance, he won by 2 min.15sec. from George, who had walked well and always held second place from Dave McMullen who suffered from cramp…

Twenty-three Club members took part in these walks and the most oustanding performance was that of Eric Hall in covering 7 miles 1635 yds. He was well backed up in the team race by N.Milsum, E.Smith and G.Checkley and we won from Met.W.C. by 36 pts. to 57.
1, K.J.Matthews(Royal Sutton Coldfield) 51m.39s; 2, E.W.Hall (Bel) 52.09; 6, N.Milsum(Bel)55.20; 8, E.A.Smith(Bel)55.43; 25, J.G.Coleman(Bel)59.58.

This was no doubt due to the fact that on the same day there occured the Police Sergeant's examination and the Stock Exchange championship. The latter event was won by Stan Vickers with Ray Hall second and Dave Stevens sixth. The match resulted in a win for us by 33 pts. to 72.
Held over the traditional Croydon to Banstead and back route of 11¾ miles, this event was notable for the eclipse of Olympic Champion Norman Read by one of our own Olympic representatives Eric Hall.

Again those two great ambassadors of the sport, Eric Hall and Stan Vickers, retained their titles in a convincing manner. A feat probably never equalled by any other club was that of ten Belgrave walkers gaining their county colours.
Soon the pace began to tell and at two miles Eric Hall had moved through and was breathing very heavily down Stan's neck with Norman Read just behind.
Comments on individuals must be headed by the continued great walking of Eric Hall who finished first. He was ably supported by George Williams 2nd, Ray Hall 6th and Terry Clark(still a junior) 8th.
Eric Hall had his first walk for over four months,when winning our opening five of the Winter Season. R.Barnes continues to improve and annexed the handicap.
2 miles Track - · 3rd. V. Thomas 13:39.0, 10th E.W. Hall 14:24: 8 18th R. Middleton 14:40.0 20th J. Knifton 14:40.6

The race was the famous Open 7 miles Walk which attracted competitors from all over the country. The bare results show that E.W. Hall placed 140th - 31st Belgravian with another two wearing claret and gold behind him.
